newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU expected to rule BA-American deal must change.
newsitem.headline: EU expected to rule BA-American deal must change.

text.p: European regulators have concluded that the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines would be anti-competitive, a source at the European Union's executive body said Tuesday.

The source said European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert would relay the decision to the British government Tuesday when he met British Trade and Industry Secretary Margaret Beckett in London to discuss the alliance.

The commission's decision had been awaited since January, when Van Miert warned the British government in a letter that the alliance would eliminate competition on many key air routes between the United States and Britain.
The commission declined official comment as is usual in large, market-sensitive alliances. But the commission may make a statement towards the end of the week, the commission source said.
British Airways said it would meet with commission officials as soon as possible to discuss the alliance, which was announced last year.

"The commission has indicated that it would like to meet us and we welcome the opportunity," a British Airways spokesman said. "We have been waiting for the commission to tell us any concerns it might have about our proposed alliance."
Van Miert has threatened the British authorities with legal action if they fail to address the commission's competition concerns.
The commission, the European Union's executive body, shares authority with Britain to review the deal between British Airways and American, which would create the world's largest airline partnership.
Under article 89 of the Treaty of Rome, it must work with the British authorities when investigating the case but, if needed, "it shall propose appropriate measures" to ensure fair competition.
The commission source said more talks were expected.
"We cannot say that this is the end," the source said.
Meanwhile, the commission said it had proposed legislation giving it clear jurisdiction over alliances between EU and non-EU airlines.
A spokesman for Van Miert said the timing of the proposal, which had been expected for two weeks, was not related to the proposed alliance between British Airways and American.
"The text is not linked to the BA-American alliance. It's pure chance in terms of calendar," Willy Helin told the commission's daily news briefing.
The news, although unofficial, pulled British Airways' stock down 18.5 pence (30 cents) to 717.5 pence ($11.77) on the London Stock Exchange.
